title: Rotorua Geothermal Parks Guide — Te Puia vs Wai-O-Tapu vs Hell's Gate
meta_desc: Discover the best Rotorua geothermal parks for families, comparing Te Puia, Wai-O-Tapu, and Hell's Gate
intro: Rotorua is home to some of New Zealand's most impressive geothermal wonders, but which park is best for your family? With prices ranging from $30 to over $100 per person, it pays to choose wisely. In this guide, we'll compare Te Puia, Wai-O-Tapu, and Hell's Gate to help you make an informed decision.

sections.heading: Overview of Rotorua Geothermal Parks
sections.body: Rotorua is a city on the North Island of New Zealand, famous for its geothermal hot springs, geysers, and mud pools. The three main geothermal parks in Rotorua are Te Puia, Wai-O-Tapu, and Hell's Gate, each offering a unique experience. Te Puia is known for its traditional Maori cultural performances, Wai-O-Tapu for its stunning natural beauty, and Hell's Gate for its mud spa and geothermal wonders.

sections.heading: Best for Families
list: Te Puia: offers a kiwi conservation center and traditional Maori performances
Wai-O-Tapu: features a variety of colorful hot springs and a chance to see the famous Lady Knox Geyser
Hell's Gate: provides a mud spa and geothermal walk, suitable for children aged 5 and above

sections.heading: Planning Your Visit
sections.body: Before visiting any of the geothermal parks, it's essential to plan ahead. Check the park's website for opening hours, prices, and any special events or closures. It's also a good idea to book your tickets in advance to avoid waiting in line. If you're traveling with a campervan, consider staying at one of the nearby campsites, such as the Rotorua Top 10 Holiday Resort, which offers convenient access to all three parks.

sections.heading: Getting There
sections.body: The drive from Auckland to Rotorua takes approximately 3 hours, while the drive from Wellington takes around 5.5 hours. If you're using public transport, you can take a bus from Auckland or Wellington to Rotorua. Once in Rotorua, you can use a taxi or shuttle service to get to the geothermal parks.

sections.heading: Accommodation Options
sections.body: Rotorua offers a wide range of accommodation options, from budget-friendly camping sites to luxury hotels. Consider staying in a family-friendly hotel, such as the Novotel Rotorua Lakeside, or rent a holiday home through a website like Bookabach. If you're looking for a more adventurous experience, you can also stay in a campervan and explore the surrounding countryside.
